title: Absolute error of a measurement
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches the specific idea that absolute error equals half the smallest unit of the instrument; the closest matches either define absolute error as a gap from the actual value or cover accuracy limits at Year 11 depth, so the new point should be added to the bank.

draft.title: Absolute error of a measurement
card: A measurement is only as exact as the smallest unit on the scale. A length given to the nearest cm could be a little more or a little less than the number shown.
The absolute error is half of the smallest unit. For a length to the nearest cm, it is \(\pm 0.5\) cm.
Write the measurement with its error. A length of 12 cm to the nearest cm is \(12 \pm 0.5\) cm. The true length is from 11.5 cm to 12.5 cm.
Example: a ruler marked in millimetres gives 7.3 cm. The smallest unit is 0.1 cm, so the absolute error is \(\pm 0.05\) cm.
draft.remember: Absolute error is half the smallest unit of the measuring scale.

a.q: A length is measured as 25 cm to the nearest cm. What is the absolute error?
a.why: The smallest unit is 1 cm, and half of that is 0.5 cm. The option of \(\pm 1\) cm is tempting, but it is the whole unit, not half.
a.clue: Take half of the smallest unit.

b.q: Tane weighs a parcel on a scale marked in 0.1 kg steps. It reads 4.6 kg. What is the range the true mass could lie in?
b.why: The smallest unit is 0.1 kg, so the absolute error is \(\pm 0.05\) kg. This gives 4.55 kg to 4.65 kg. The range 4.5 kg to 4.7 kg uses the whole unit as the error.
b.clue: Find the smallest unit first, then halve it.
